01

About Me

It started with a simple question I couldn’t put down: who does the system leave behind, and what would it take to reach them?

That question led me to build eight systems: OncoSense, a sub-$600 AI ultrasound for cancer screening. A brain-controlled wheelchair. An on-device melanoma classifier. A robotic arm. A virtual typing system. An object distance reader. A gun detection model. Each one started because someone was falling through the cracks. These projects have been recognized on national and international stages.

As the Programming Technical Reference for FRC Team 9277, I competed at the FIRST Robotics World Championship and learned that strong technology only solves half the problem. Getting it into the right hands takes vision, mentorship, and business thinking I never expected to need.

I serve as a board member of the Youth Advisory at the Alberta Children’s Hospital, a Flight Corporal in the Air Cadets, and a member of the Mayor’s Youth Council. At the Young Canadians Parliament, I spoke with the Honourable Mark Miller about social media safety. I have also run more than 40 free coding and math workshops for kids. Technology does not fix problems on its own. People do. In my journey, I weaponize the challenges I face, turning adversity into solutions.

Portable AI ultrasound · CYSF 2025 Gold Medal

OncoSense: Portable AI Multi-Cancer Screening

An affordable, sub-$600 handheld ultrasound system combining custom pulser/receiver circuitry, a 5MHz transducer, and a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller with a Jetson Nano 4GB running real-time YOLOv8 segmentation. Delivers 95% accuracy screening for breast, liver (HCC), and papillary thyroid cancers in underserved rural populations.

The Skin Screener
